newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan minister says difficult judgments needed.
newsitem.headline: Japan minister says difficult judgments needed.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda on Tuesday called off a visit to South Korea and said "difficult judgments" were needed on how to end the hostage crisis in Lima.
"After consulting Prime Minister (Ryutaro) Hashimoto and the South Korean government, I decided to cancel my visit scheduled for December 26 and 27," Ikeda told a news conference.

Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on December 17 during a reception to mark Emperor Akihito's birthday, taking more than 500 hostages.
After freeing a large number of captives, the rebels were still holding at gunpoint dozens of top Peruvian government officials and about 30 high-ranking Japanese businessmen and diplomats.
"We are entering a stage which requires us to make difficult judgments," Ikeda said. "We will seek the release of the remaining hostages as soon as possible."
Ikeda spent four days in Lima as Japan's on-the-spot adviser and returned to Tokyo on Monday evening.

The foreign minister had planned to hold talks with his South Korean counterpart Yoo Chong-ha ahead of a summit meeting in Japan in late January between Hashimoto and South Korean President Kim Young-sam.

Ikeda said he did not even rule out the possibility that the hostage crisis could force the cancellation of the summit meeting in the resort city of Beppu on Japan's southernmost main island of Kyushu on January 25 and 26.
"It all hinges on the developments in the incident in Peru," Ikeda said.
